questions.question: In the circuit shown in figure, what value of C will cause a unity power factor at the ac source?
questions.explanation:
\(Y=j\omega C+\frac{1}{30\angle 40^{\circ}}\)
\(\;\;=j\omega C+0.0255-j0.0214\)
\(\;\;=0.0255+j(\omega C-0.0214)\)

questions.subject: electric-circuits
questions.question:
A first order, low pass filter is given with R=50 \(\Omega\) and C=\(5\mu F\). What is the
frequency at which the gain of the voltage transfer function of the filter is 0.25?
questions.explanation:
\(T.F.=\frac{V_o}{V_i}=\frac{\frac{1}{j\omega C}}{R+\frac{1}{j\omega C}}\)
\(\;\;\;=\frac{1}{1+j\omega CR}\)
\(\therefore \; \; |Gain|=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+(\omega CR)^2}}\)
\(\;\;0.25=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+(\omega \times 5 \times 10^{-6} \times 50)^2}}\)
On solving,
\(\omega =15.49 \times 10^3 r/s\)
\(\Rightarrow \;\; f=\frac{15.49}{2 \pi}=2.46 kHz\)

questions.subject: electric-circuits
questions.question: A series R-L-C circuit has R=\(50\Omega\), L=\(100\mu\) and C=\(1\mu\). The lower half power frequency of the circuit is
questions.explanation:
\(\omega _0=\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}\)
\(\;\;=\frac{1}{\sqrt{100 \times 10^{-6} \times 10^{-6}}}=10^5 r/s\)
\(\Delta \omega =\frac{R}{L}=\frac{50}{100 \times 10^{-6}}\)
\(\;\;=50 \times 10^4 r/s\)
\(\omega _{lower}=\left [ \sqrt{\omega _0^2+\left ( \frac{\Delta \omega }{2} \right )^2}- \frac{\Delta \omega }{2}\right ]\)
\(\;\;=\left [ \sqrt{(10^5)^2+\left ( \frac{5 \times 10^5}{2} \right )^2}-\frac{5 \times 10^5}{2} \right ]\)
\(\;\;=10^5\left [ \sqrt{1+6.25}-2.5 \right ]\)
\(\;\;=0.193 \times 10^5 r/s\)
Hence, \(f_{lower}=\frac{\omega _{lower}}{2 \pi}\)
\(\;\;=\frac{0.193 \times 10^5}{2 \pi}\)
\(\;\;=3065 Hz\approx 3.055kHz\)

questions.question: For the system \[\dot{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0\\ 0&4 \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix} u; y=\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}X\], with u as unit impulse and with zero initial state, the output, y, becomes
questions.explanation:
\(x(t)=e^{At}X(0)+\int_{0}^{t}e^{A(t-\tau) }BU(\tau )d\tau\)
\(\because \;\; X(0)=0\) (as given)
\[\therefore \;\; x(t)=0+\int_{0}^{t}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2(t-\tau )} &0 \\ 0 & e^{4(t-\tau )} \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\delta (t)dt\]
\[\;\;=\int_{0}^{t}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2(t-\tau )}\\ e^{2(t-\tau )} \end{bmatrix}\delta (t)dt\]
\[\;\;=\begin{bmatrix} e^{2t}\\ e^{4t} \end{bmatrix}\]
Output \[y(t)=\begin{bmatrix} 4 &0 \end{bmatrix}x(t)\]
\[\;\;=\begin{bmatrix} 4 &0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} e^{2t}\\ e^{4t} \end{bmatrix}\]
Hence, \(y(t)=4e^{2t}\)

\(\frac{\Delta L}{2}=I_{L(avg)}=I_{0(avg)}\)
this is applicable only at the boundary of continuous and discontinuous
\[\begin{aligned} L_c &=\frac{\alpha V_s(1-\alpha )}{2I_0f} \\ L_c&=\frac{\alpha V_sR(1-\alpha )}{R2I_0f} \\ (\because & \text{ multiplying and dividing by R}) \\ L_c&=\frac{V_0 R(1-\alpha )}{RI_02f} \\ L_c&= \frac{I_0R(1-\alpha )}{I_02f}\\ L_c&=\frac{R(1-\alpha )}{2f} \\ \therefore &= \text{ Boundary value of duty cycle is,}\\ \frac{2fL}{R}&=1-\alpha \\ \alpha &= 1-\frac{2fL}{R}=1-\frac{2L}{RT} \end{aligned}\]
